_comment: Edit with the user's approval only. 'terms' = advanced words that need a plain gloss in the SAME paragraph at their first use in a file (gloss = parentheses right after the term, or words like 'means', 'i.e.', 'that is', 'in other words', 'called', 'a dash/colon definition'). 'banned' = names the user rejected; always use the replacement.

terms.non-centrality: how far the test statistic is pushed up by a real effect
terms.noncentrality: how far the test statistic is pushed up by a real effect
terms.type i error: a false alarm: rejecting when there is no real effect
terms.type ii error: a miss: failing to reject when there is a real effect
terms.false negative: a miss: failing to reject when there is a real effect
terms.statistical power: how often the test catches a real effect
terms.observational equivalence: different parameter sets that produce the same data behaviour
terms.identification: whether the parameters can be pinned down uniquely from data
terms.unidentified: whose parameters cannot be pinned down uniquely from data
terms.invertib: whether the moving-average part can be rewritten as an autoregression
terms.kullback: a measure of how far a model is from the true data-generating process
terms.nested: one model is the other with some coefficients set to zero
terms.null hypothesis: the 'no effect' assumption the test tries to reject
terms.critical value: the cut-off the test statistic must beat to reject
terms.residual sum of squares: the total squared forecast error left over
terms.degrees of freedom: the number of independent data points left after estimating coefficients
terms.cointegrat: series that wander apart but are pulled back to a long-run relationship
terms.innovation: the new, unpredictable shock at each step
terms.autocovariance: how a series moves together with its own past
terms.asymptotic: what happens with a very large sample
terms.eigenvalue: a number that tells whether shocks die out or grow
terms.unit root: a stochastic trend that never reverts

banned.detection rate: Granger rejection rate (or: % of datasets where Granger rejects)
banned.detection power: how often the test catches a real effect
banned.median detection threshold: the b where a typical dataset first clears the Granger bar
